purpose: Zavegepant is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It works to relieve migraine pain and symptoms like nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. It is not used to prevent migraines, only to treat them when one starts.
how_it_works: During a migraine, your body releases a protein called CGRP that causes blood vessels in the brain to widen and sends pain signals. Zavegepant blocks the receptor that CGRP attaches to, which helps stop those pain signals. Think of it like putting a lock on a door so the migraine trigger cannot get in.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is an unusual taste in your mouth (like a bitter or metallic taste) after using the nasal spray. Some people may also notice nasal discomfort, throat irritation, or nausea. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as this medication may not be right for you. Avoid using it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first. Do not use it more than once in a 24-hour period. If your migraine does not improve, contact your healthcare provider before taking another dose.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one spray (10 mg) into one nostril at the start of a migraine. You can only use one dose in a 24-hour period. It comes as a nasal spray, so no swallowing pills is needed, which can be helpful if nausea makes it hard to take tablets.
